experiment.question: Does ready capacity remove the burst loss, or does steady-state capacity remain inadequate?

app.placement: Same pod UIDs and original two nodes verified before each arm

experiment.acceptance: No dropped scheduled requests, controlled end-to-end latency, no errors, complete recovery, natural return to two Ready nodes; a diagnostic A/B alone is not a proven production fix.
caveats: Cache readiness and backend connection distribution are part of warm-versus-scale-up cost.
Updated_since is generated relative to wall clock in both arms.
One pair is diagnostic; a successful candidate requires repetition.
250m held constant because the 1-CPU candidate did not fit the two-node idle requirement.

generator.scope: Whole four-vCPU generator from /proc/stat and non-loopback network devices; includes monitoring overhead. CPU busy includes steal, reported separately. Does not alone rule out single-thread or network constraints.

database_statement_deltas.scope: Only statements present in both bounded top-25 snapshots; interval brackets burst with collection padding

recovery_refusal.interpretation: Refusal occurred during ingress downscaling; endpoint on tbww changes to terminating near the failure while LB health still reports healthy. No packet capture identifies the rejecting backend; causation is not established.

verdict: Both burst gates failed; neither arm establishes a production fix.
measurement_limitations: Measured v4 driver retained complete failure totals but only 100 individual failure samples; later reset timestamps were omitted.
A subsequent driver commit adds complete per-window error-class counts for future runs; it was not used in either measured arm.
PostgreSQL statement deltas bracket preparation, burst and early recovery; they are not precise per-burst SQL statistics.
Origin gauges are sampled every 60 seconds; brief events may be missed.
